replacements.ground: At HEAD both clauses read "will carry", which is dispositional: if hunger comes the stores suffice, and if plague comes nothing here does. replacements.headText: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one, and knows which of the two it fears.

replacements.now: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one. The town knows the sick year is the one it fears.
replacements.ground: The cut's new sentence dropped a HEAD claim as well as adding one: HEAD asserted that the town KNOWS which of the two it fears, which licenses a game master to stage a townsperson answering that question straight, and "It is the sick year the town fears" says nothing about the town's settled self-knowledge. Restoring "knows" costs no clarity and puts that half of the delta back, while 42b still forbids returning to HEAD's vague tail, so the definite "the sick year" stays, the split into two sentences stays (the second carries a real fact and so earns its place under 42a), and the line is also listed under sharpenings42b with the full two-way delta for the refuter.

sharpenings42b.nowText: The town can outlast a hungry year at {settlement} and has no answer at all to a sick one. The town knows the sick year is the one it fears.

sharpenings42b.whyThePoolStateSupportsIt: HEAD's tail names no fear and so makes no claim a reader can act on, the textbook 42b failure, and the pool's own state settles which reading is lawful: the grain store is present, so a failed harvest is survivable, and there is no medical provision of any kind, so of the two years named in the same sentence only the sick one is uncovered. The alternative reading would contradict the first half of its own sentence. The line as repaired hands the refuter the WHOLE delta rather than half of it: the sharpening ADDS which year is feared, and my repair RESTORES the town's knowledge of it, so the refuter must test both, and in particular whether the card supports attributing a fear, and knowledge of that fear, to the town as a body at all rather than only the two capability facts.

result.summary: Ten replacements, all of them claim restorations that keep the cut's clarity gains. Six come straight from the chair's section A classes: two stranded attributions re-joined or re-attributed (v1 face 3, v2 face 5), three actor or scope changes put back (v1 face 9's 'his' to 'the garrison's', v2 face 1's added hall-as-keeper, v2 face 2's shrunk beneficiary class), and the invented sentence 'The table can put a name to him' cut from v3 face 2. V3 face 7 is restored to HEAD's habitual and to HEAD's actor, the town, under A1 read together with A4, giving up the 42d stake because it cannot be carried in the present tense without narrowing HEAD's indefinite 'a question'. Three more are of the same classes and were missed by the auditors or filed only as notes: v1 face 5's 'his night round' back to 'the night round', v3 face 8's 'never told' back to 'are not told', and v2 face 8's gloss verb 'reckon' back to 'say'.
